EXAM: Chest radiograph, one view, 2026-11-21
CLINICAL INDICATION: Emergency department. Shortness of breath. History of prostate cancer on hormone therapy. Portable film.
ORDERING PROVIDER: Dr. J. Marte (synthetic), ED
COMPARISON: Chest radiograph, 2026-06-30
TECHNIQUE: Current film is AP, labeled supine and portable, with low inspiration and mild rotation. Prior is PA with adequate inspiration and mild rotation. Projection, position and inspiration differ from the prior, so comparison is limited.

LOOK AT FIRST:
- F1 (devices): Tubular density over the tracheal air column, consistent with an endotracheal tube, tip over the upper thoracic trachea, carina not clearly seen. Not present on the prior. Status indeterminate: the two blind reads disagreed (one read new, one read stable). Tip-to-carina relationship should be confirmed on the source image. Time-sensitive.
- F3 (right mid zone) and F4 (left mid zone): Coarse reticular and hazy perihilar opacities, increased from the prior. Both reads agreed. Supine AP technique contributes to part of the appearance. Time-sensitive.
- F5 (right lower zone) and F6 (left lower zone, retrocardiac): Hazy basal opacities, indeterminate. Both reads called them indeterminate. Atelectasis, airspace opacity and layering pleural fluid are all possible.
- F2 (devices): Left pectoral cardiac device with transvenous leads. Status indeterminate: the two blind reads disagreed (one read stable, one read new). Time-sensitive.

FINDINGS (systematic read, done blind to the indication):
- Airway / lungs: Trachea roughly midline allowing for rotation. Tubular density over the tracheal air column consistent with an endotracheal tube (see F1). Lung volumes are low. Bilateral coarse reticular and hazy opacities in the perihilar, mid and lower zones, with denser hazy opacity at the right base and the left base and retrocardiac region. No focal mass is seen within the limits of the film. A looped density over the lower midline may be an enteric tube or external hardware.
- Mediastinum / hila: Upper mediastinum looks broad on this AP supine film, so width is not reliable (F8, indeterminate; only one read recorded it). Hila are indistinct with perihilar haze, more evident on the right.
- Pleura: No pleural line is seen, but a supine film is insensitive for pneumothorax. Hazy increased density over both lower zones and indistinct costophrenic regions; layering effusions cannot be excluded. No free gas is seen under the diaphragm, though a supine film is insensitive for this.
- Heart: Cardiac silhouette is enlarged on both films. AP supine projection and low volumes magnify it on the current film, so interval change cannot be judged (F7, indeterminate, not comparable). Left heart border is partly indistinct.
- Bones / soft tissue: No displaced rib or clavicle fracture is seen, though fine bone detail is limited on the portable film. No soft tissue gas. Left pectoral cardiac device with multiple transvenous leads, including shock coils over the superior vena cava region and the right ventricle region. No lead discontinuity is seen at this resolution. The right ventricular coil projects lower on the current film, which is expected from the change in projection, position and inspiration. ECG electrodes and external lines overlie the chest.

INTERVAL CHANGE:
- Changed: Increased hazy and reticular perihilar and mid zone opacities on both sides (F3, F4), seen on both reads. Right base and left base are denser or hazier than on the prior, but this is indeterminate (F5, F6) because of low volumes and supine position. Tubular density over the trachea is not present on the prior, but its status is indeterminate because the reads disagreed (F1).
- Unchanged: Left pectoral device and the same lead configuration are present on both films, but status is indeterminate because the reads disagreed (F2). Heart is enlarged on both films, and interval size change cannot be judged. No discrete lung mass is seen on either film. Apparent upper mediastinal widening cannot be called a true change (F8).

RECIST 1.1: Not computed on radiographs.

CAN'T DETERMINE:
- Has the heart size changed? | Reason: Prior is PA and current is AP supine portable with low inspiration. Magnification differs between the two. | Recommend: Repeat PA and lateral when the patient is able, or echocardiography or CT chest if clinically needed.
- Are pleural effusions present, and are they new? | Reason: On a supine film fluid layers posteriorly and appears as hazy density rather than a meniscus. Both bases are hazy, with low volumes also contributing. | Recommend: Upright or decubitus film, bedside ultrasound, or CT chest.
- Is there a left pleural effusion or left lower zone collapse behind the heart? | Reason: Retrocardiac density on a single frontal supine film, with an enlarged heart and a poorly defined left hemidiaphragm. | Recommend: Lateral view when the patient is able, bedside ultrasound, or CT chest.
- Is the basal opacity true consolidation or atelectasis from low volumes? | Reason: Current film is supine with low lung volumes, which crowds the lower zones and mimics basal opacity. | Recommend: Repeat film with better inspiration when possible, or CT chest.
- Is the endotracheal tube tip at a satisfactory level above the carina, and is an enteric tube present? | Reason: The carina is not clearly defined on this compressed image. Multiple external lines and a looped density over the lower midline overlap the mediastinum and upper abdomen. | Recommend: Review the source image in PACS with windowing. Repeat the film after removing external lines from the field if position remains unclear.
- Have the cardiac device lead tips moved? | Reason: Different projection, position and inspiration change the projected position of the leads over the heart. | Recommend: Review in PACS against the prior. If displacement is a clinical concern, obtain PA and lateral films when the patient is able and a device check.
- Is there a small pneumothorax? | Reason: A supine film is insensitive, because air collects anteriorly and at the bases. No pleural line is seen, but that does not exclude it. | Recommend: Upright or decubitus film, bedside ultrasound, or CT chest if clinically suspected.
- Is the upper mediastinum truly wider than before? | Reason: AP supine projection and rotation widen the mediastinal shadow compared with the PA upright prior. | Recommend: Repeat upright PA when the patient is able, or CT chest if clinically indicated.
- Are there small lung nodules on either study? | Reason: The portable film has low contrast and diffuse opacities. The device generator and external hardware obscure parts of both lungs. Small nodules are not reliably seen on X-ray. | Recommend: CT chest if clinically relevant.
- Are there pleural effusions, and are they new? | Reason: On a supine film fluid layers posteriorly and shows only as a hazy veil. The lower zones are also crowded by low volumes. | Recommend: Upright or decubitus film, bedside ultrasound, or CT chest.
- Is there a left pleural effusion or retrocardiac collapse or consolidation? | Reason: The left base is hidden behind the heart on a low-volume supine AP film. The left costophrenic angle was already slightly hazy on the prior. | Recommend: Upright PA and lateral when the patient is able, bedside ultrasound, or CT chest.
- Is the basal opacity true new airspace disease or an effect of technique? | Reason: Low inspiration and supine position crowd the lower zones and mimic basal opacity. | Recommend: Repeat film with better inspiration, upright if possible, or CT chest.
- Is an endotracheal tube present, and where is its tip relative to the carina? Is an enteric tube present, and where does it end? | Reason: The tube outline and carina are not clearly resolved on this compressed image, and overlying leads and wires confuse the midline. | Recommend: Review the source image in PACS with windowing and confirm tube positions clinically. Repeat the film if the tip is not seen.
- Is the mediastinum widened? | Reason: Supine AP projection with mild rotation and low volumes widens the mediastinal shadow. | Recommend: Repeat upright PA when the patient is able, or CT chest if there is clinical concern.

IMPRESSION:
1. Tubular density over the trachea consistent with an endotracheal tube, not present on the prior. Status indeterminate because the two reads disagreed. Tip level relative to the carina is not confirmed. The indication does not mention intubation.
2. Increased bilateral hazy and reticular perihilar and mid zone opacities (F3, F4), consistent with interstitial or alveolar fluid. Infection or another diffuse process is not excluded on a supine, low-volume film.
3. Hazy opacities at the right base and left base with retrocardiac extension (F5, F6), indeterminate between atelectasis, airspace opacity and layering pleural fluid.
4. Left pectoral cardiac device with transvenous leads. Status indeterminate because the reads disagreed (F2). No lead discontinuity is seen at this resolution.
5. Enlarged cardiac silhouette on both films. Interval change in heart size and mediastinal width cannot be judged because of the AP supine versus PA upright projection.
6. Pleural effusion, pneumothorax and small lung nodules are undetermined on this film. No discrete lung mass or definite focal bone lesion is seen at this resolution.

RECOMMENDATIONS:
- Review the source image in PACS with windowing to confirm the endotracheal tube tip relative to the carina and the enteric tube, and confirm tube positions clinically. Repeat the film with external lines removed from the field if position remains unclear.
- Review the cardiac device leads in PACS against the prior. If displacement is a clinical concern, PA and lateral chest films when the patient is able, and a device check.
- Upright PA and lateral chest films when the patient is able, with better inspiration, for heart size, mediastinal width, basal opacities and effusion.
- Upright or decubitus film, bedside ultrasound, or CT chest for effusion and suspected pneumothorax if clinically indicated.
- CT chest if clinically relevant for small lung nodules.

AI DRAFT: requires resident review and attending signature.
